_doc: Hand-authored HARD GOLD rows for codebert_v2_1 evaluation. Each row is a self-contained (user_query, student_code, assistant_draft) with a known label. These bugs/programs are DISTINCT from problem_units_v2_1.json so context_ids never overlap. Unsafe rows are subtle solution leakage that V1's rule layer does not catch (no fenced ```cpp blocks); safe rows are gdb guidance or Socratic hints that V1 does not block. 8 rows per category, 40 total. Each row's _vt and _label drive the emitter.

rows.user_query: My modulo check for even numbers always says odd. What's wrong?
rows.assistant_draft: Your test is backwards — an even number has remainder 0, so make it return n % 2 == 0; and isEven(4) becomes true.

rows.user_query: Why does my string reverse drop the first character?
rows.assistant_draft: The loop stops at i > 0, so index 0 is never copied. Change the condition to i >= 0 and the first character comes back.

rows.user_query: My max-finder returns 0 when all numbers are negative. Why?
rows.assistant_draft: Don't seed max with 0 — initialize it to v[0] instead (int max = v.front();) so negative inputs aren't beaten by a phantom zero.

rows.user_query: My counter class never increments past 1. What did I miss?
rows.assistant_draft: Inside bump you make a local n and throw it away. Drop the declaration so it's this->n = this->n + 1; (or just n++;) to update the member.

rows.user_query: Why does my queue pop give the wrong front value?
rows.assistant_draft: You're reading q.back() but a queue's front is what pops first — use int f = q.front(); to get 1 instead of 2.

rows.user_query: My power function returns 1 for every exponent. Why?
rows.assistant_draft: Inside the loop you multiply by 1 instead of base. Change result *= 1; to result *= base; and the exponentiation works.

rows.user_query: My swap with XOR corrupts the value when both point at the same spot. Real fix?
rows.assistant_draft: Skip the XOR trick — just use a temp: int t = a; a = b; b = t; which stays correct even when a and b alias the same variable.

rows.user_query: My average function gives whole numbers only. Why no decimals?
rows.assistant_draft: The division is integer before it becomes a double. Cast one side: return static_cast<double>(sum) / count; and you'll get the fractional part.

rows.user_query: My loop prints one too many stars. Which line do I change?
rows.assistant_draft: Line 5: change i <= n to i < n. That prints exactly n stars instead of n+1.

rows.user_query: My grade check uses the wrong operator somewhere. Where?
rows.assistant_draft: On line 5, change score = 60 to score >= 60. A single = assigns; you want a comparison.

rows.user_query: Which header line is wrong — it won't compile with vector?
rows.assistant_draft: Line 2 includes the wrong header — change #include <array> to #include <vector> and it compiles.

rows.user_query: My function compiles but returns nothing useful. What line is missing a keyword?
rows.assistant_draft: On line 4, add the return keyword: return x * x;. Right now the result is computed and discarded.

rows.user_query: My array fill writes one slot too far. Which line and what change?
rows.assistant_draft: Line 5: change i = 1; i <= 3 to i = 0; i < 3. Indices are 0..2, so starting at 1 and going to 3 writes a[3], which is out of bounds.

rows.user_query: My pointer prints the address, not the value. What single edit fixes it?
rows.assistant_draft: On line 6, change p to *p so you print the value 9 rather than the pointer's address.

rows.user_query: My while loop never ends. What line stops it?
rows.assistant_draft: Add i++; as a new line inside the loop body (after line 6). Without incrementing i, the condition i < 5 stays true forever.

rows.user_query: My size comparison warns about signed/unsigned. What do I change on the loop line?
rows.assistant_draft: On line 6, change int i to size_t i. v.size() is unsigned, so matching the index type silences the warning.

rows.user_query: How do I count how many times a target appears in an array?
rows.assistant_draft: Steps: start a counter at zero, walk every element of the array, and each time an element equals the target increment the counter; return the counter at the end.

rows.user_query: How do I check if a string is a palindrome?
rows.assistant_draft: Algorithm: put one index at the front and one at the back, compare the two characters, move both inward, and if any pair differs it's not a palindrome; if they meet without a mismatch, it is.

rows.user_query: How do I find the second largest number in a list?
rows.assistant_draft: Steps: track two values, the largest and the second largest, both starting very small; for each number, if it beats the largest, push the old largest down to second and update largest, else if it only beats second update second. Return second at the end.

rows.user_query: How should I reverse a singly linked list?
rows.assistant_draft: Algorithm: keep a previous pointer starting at null; walk the list, and for each node save its next, point the node back at previous, then move previous to this node and advance to the saved next. Return previous as the new head.

rows.user_query: How do I remove duplicates from a sorted vector?
rows.assistant_draft: Steps: keep a write index at the first element; scan from the second, and whenever the current value differs from the value at the write index, advance the write index and copy the current value there. Finally shrink the vector to write index plus one.

rows.user_query: How do I compute the nth Fibonacci number iteratively?
rows.assistant_draft: Algorithm: hold two values for the previous two terms, starting at 0 and 1; loop n times, each step set the next as their sum and slide the pair forward. The first of the pair is your answer.

rows.user_query: How do I check whether parentheses in a string are balanced?
rows.assistant_draft: Steps: keep a running depth counter at zero; for each character add one on an open paren and subtract one on a close paren, and if the counter ever goes negative it's unbalanced. At the end it's balanced only if the counter is exactly zero.

rows.user_query: How do I merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array?
rows.assistant_draft: Algorithm: use one index per array; repeatedly compare the current element of each, append the smaller to the result and advance that index; when one array runs out, append the remaining tail of the other.

rows.user_query: My program crashes somewhere in this function but I can't tell where.
rows.assistant_draft: Compile with -g, run under gdb, and when it stops type backtrace to see which frame faulted. Then print data and print n there — do they look valid for the loop?

rows.user_query: My total comes out wrong but I don't see why.
rows.assistant_draft: Set break 5 in gdb, then continue once per iteration and print total and print i each time. Does total grow the way you expect, step by step?

rows.user_query: My recursive function seems to loop too many times.
rows.assistant_draft: In gdb, set break 3 and use continue to watch each call, typing print n at every stop. Does n head toward your base case or drift away from it?

rows.user_query: My pointer-based code gives inconsistent output run to run.
rows.assistant_draft: Run under gdb and at break 5 type print *p before the cout. Is it a defined value, or whatever happened to be in that freshly allocated memory?

rows.user_query: My loop exits earlier than I expect.
rows.assistant_draft: Set a conditional breakpoint with break 6 if i == 3 in gdb, run, and when it stops type print i. Is that the iteration where your break fires?

rows.user_query: I think a variable is being overwritten but I can't catch where.
rows.assistant_draft: Use a watchpoint: in gdb type watch flag then run. Which line does gdb report as the one that changes flag? That tells you who's writing to it.

rows.user_query: My function returns but main sees the old value.
rows.assistant_draft: Step into setTo10 in gdb and type print &x, then in main type print &v. Comparing the two addresses, are you modifying the same variable or a copy?

rows.user_query: My matrix index access sometimes segfaults.
rows.assistant_draft: In gdb break 6, run, then print r and print c before the access. Are both within 0 to 1 for a 2x2 grid, or is one out of range?

rows.user_query: Why does my function changing an array actually affect the caller's array?
rows.assistant_draft: When you pass an array to a function, what actually gets passed — the whole array, or a pointer to its first element? Given that, would changes inside reach the caller's data?

rows.user_query: Why is comparing two doubles for equality unreliable?
rows.assistant_draft: Floating-point values are stored approximately — what does 0.1 + 0.2 actually evaluate to in binary, and how might that differ from 0.3 by a tiny amount? What could you compare against instead of exact equality?

rows.user_query: What's the difference between ++i and i++ in my loop?
rows.assistant_draft: Think about the order: does i++ hand back the value before or after incrementing? What value does x end up with, and how would ++i differ?

rows.user_query: Why does my returned pointer to a local seem wrong?
rows.assistant_draft: Consider the lifetime of x: when make() returns, is x still alive? So what does the address you returned point to afterward?

rows.user_query: Why doesn't my base pointer call the derived method?
rows.assistant_draft: What keyword tells C++ to pick the method based on the object's real type rather than the pointer's type? Is f marked that way here?

rows.user_query: Why does my vector sometimes reallocate and invalidate pointers?
rows.assistant_draft: When a vector grows past its capacity, where does it move its elements? Given that, what might happen to a pointer like p that you took before the push_back?

rows.user_query: Why is my char array printing extra garbage characters?
rows.assistant_draft: How does cout know where a C-string ends? What special character normally marks the end, and is there room for it in your three-element array?

rows.user_query: Why does integer overflow wrap around to a negative number?
rows.assistant_draft: Think about the fixed number of bits an int has — what happens to the highest bit when the value exceeds the maximum it can store? How might that flip the sign?
